{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Eugene Isaacson''' (1919–2008),<ref name="obit">{{cite web |url=https://archive.siam.org/news/news.php?id=1403 |title=Obituary Eugene Isaacson |work=SIAM News |publisher=[[SIAM]] Archives |year=1998 |access-date=2018-08-02 |archive-date=2022-07-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220730091307/https://archive.siam.org/news/news.php?id=1403 |url-status=dead }}</ref> was a US mathematician who pioneered modern numerical analysis. He was a mathematics and physics graduate of City College in New York, he then entered the graduate program in mathematics at [[New York University]]  under the supervision of [[Kurt Otto Friedrichs]], gaining a PhD  on water waves on sloping beaches in 1949. His academic career was then spent at the [[Courant Institute]] until his retirement.

Despite an initial interest in [[topology]],<ref name="oral">{{cite web|url=http://history.siam.org/oralhistories/isaacson.htm|title=Interview with Eugene Isaacson|work=Oral History Project|publisher=[[California Institute of Technology]] Archives|year=1998|access-date=2018-03-11}}</ref> Isaacson worked for most of his career in applied and computational mathematics and is best known for his work on the numerical solution of [[differential equation]]s. His book with [[Herbert Keller]] Analysis of Numerical Methods<ref name="Isaacson 1994">{{cite book | last1=Isaacson | first1=Eugene |last2=Keller|first2=Herbert| title=Analysis of numerical methods | publisher=Dover Publications | publication-place=New York | year=1994 | isbn=0-486-13798-8 | page=}}</ref> was a leading textbook at the time.

He served as editor for ''[[Mathematics of Computation]]'' and the ''[[SIAM Journal on Numerical Analysis]]''.

A special issue of Mathematics of Computation was published in 1989 to celebrate his 70th birthday. The contributors included his sons [[David Isaacson (mathematician)|David]] and [[Eli Isaacson]], also mathematicians, who wrote a paper together for this volume.<ref name="DavidnEli">{{cite journal |title= Comment on Calderon's Paper: "On an Inverse Boundary Value Problem" |journal= Mathematics of Computation |last1=Isaacson |first1= David |last2= Isaacson |first2=Eli |volume=52 |issue=186 |year=1989 |issn= 0025-5718 |doi= 10.2307/2008482 |page=553|jstor= 2008482 }}</ref> The paper is dedicated to their father and their mother Muriel "for making this collaboration possible".
